title: Noor and the Signal
premise: Lena Quintana, a xenolinguist whose dreams have slowly been replaced by an alien signal she can't translate, keeps a lonely beacon on the edge of the Meridian War. When the salvage ship Vespera returns from deep space with its crew biologically aged backward, Lena is conscripted to decode the message they carry — one that proves the war's founding atrocity was staged by both governments. As factions hunt the crew and the beacon becomes a target, Lena must choose between protecting her found family aboard the Vespera and broadcasting a truth that could shatter the fragile armistice. In the end, she transmits the message through the beacon itself, sacrificing her connection to the signal and her career, but buying the galaxy a chance at real peace.
about_author: Yara Vasquez is a former radio astronomer turned novelist who writes about the people history forgets — the technicians, translators, and caretakers of humanity's machines. She lives near an decommissioned listening station and insists the static there sounds like language.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On the frigid relay station Kestrel-9, Lena maintains a beacon whose commissioning records have vanished, speaking maintenance logs aloud in languages that stopped being human years ago. A supply run brings news of the Vespera's impossible return. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into dread as she realizes the signal in her dreams has changed pitch.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Vespera captain Odile Ferro's POV. The ship docks under military quarantine; its crew of veterans now has the bodies of twenty-year-olds and memories of forty more years than their cells admit. Odile hides a data core sewn into her jacket lining. Emotional beat: disorientation and fierce protectiveness toward a crew the government wants to dissect.

chapters.title: Conscription Papers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A Ministry liaison arrives at Kestrel-9 with orders: Lena's linguistic anomalies make her the only qualified decoder for the Vespera's cargo. She protests, then sees the liaison's file on herself — flagged, watched, dreamed-about. Emotional beat: the chill of discovering she was never forgotten, only stored.

chapters.title: First Contact, Second Hand
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lena meets the de-aged crew in a holding ward; engineer Tam Rhee, now physically nineteen, recognizes her voice from a transmission he heard 'thirty' years ago. The data core resists every standard decryption. Emotional beat: uncanny kinship between two people out of sync with time.

chapters.title: What the Signal Wants
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Working nights, Lena realizes the core isn't encrypted — it's linguistic, addressed in the same grammar her dreams have been rehearsing for a decade. It contains coordinates and a phrase she translates as 'witness us.' Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of being chosen by something vast.

chapters.title: The Staged Atrocity
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Decoded fragments reveal the Cassini Station massacre that started the Meridian War was manufactured — falsified telemetry planted by both sides' intelligence services. Odile decides the message must go public, not to any government. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Loyalty Audit
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Ministry interrogators pressure Tam to report his captain's intentions, dangling restorative treatment for his stolen youth. He stalls, torn between decades of loyalty to Odile and the seductive promise of getting his life back. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Kestrel Burns
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Saboteurs destroy the beacon station to bury the decoding work; Lena escapes with only her dream-journals and the partial translation key in her head. The liaison dies saving her — or so it appears. Emotional beat: loss of the last place that was hers.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Lena reaches the impounded Vespera; the crew votes to smuggle her aboard rather than surrender the translation. They steal their own ship out of drydock during a solar storm. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing around a fugitive stranger.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. In transit, the crew must stay radio-dark while both navies hunt them. Boredom breeds confession: Tam admits the interrogation, expecting exile, and Odile instead gives him the core to guard. Emotional beat: forgiveness as an act of trust, not absolution.

chapters.title: Dream Grammar
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Sleep-deprived, Lena finally dreams the full sentence the signal has been building: the aliens witnessed the staged massacre and are returning to demand justice — with a deadline measured in orbital mechanics, not diplomacy. Emotional beat: the weight of being the only mouth for a dying species' testimony.

chapters.title: Two Flags, One Bounty
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Both governments offer amnesty for the core and death for the crew; a former ally sells their route to the highest bidder. The Vespera takes damage limping through a minefield toward the neutral archive moon of Halcyon Reach. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institutions they once served.

chapters.title: Halcyon Reach
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The archive moon's archivists — exiles, deserters, and record-keepers — agree to authenticate the massacre evidence but warn that publication requires a live broadcast from an authorized beacon. There is exactly one left: Kestrel-9, supposedly destroyed. Emotional beat: hope arriving with a catch.

chapters.title: The Liaison's Ghost
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The 'dead' liaison, Minister-Adjunct Corvane, contacts them: he faked his death and reveals the sabotage order came from above him. He offers fleet codes for Kestrel-9's backup array — if Lena lets him control the broadcast. Emotional beat: truth offered wrapped in ambition.

chapters.title: Split Vote
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The crew fractures: some want Corvane's codes, others a pirate relay that might not reach civilian channels. Tam casts the deciding vote for Corvane, betting his restored future on the man who once tried to buy him. Emotional beat: choosing trust as strategy, not sentiment.

chapters.title: Running the Cordon
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Vespera races back toward Kestrel-9 through a joint navy cordon, using the de-aged crew's intimate knowledge of their own older tactics against their pursuers. Casualties mount; the med bay runs out of synthetic plasma. Emotional beat: sacrifice made ordinary by necessity.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Boarding the ruined beacon, Lena discovers why it was built: it was always meant to carry this message, commissioned decades ago by whistleblowers who were silenced before launch. Her whole exile was someone else's contingency plan. Emotional beat: rage transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Price
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the array, Corvane reveals he intends to edit the broadcast — blame assigned cleanly to one side, himself the hero of disclosure. Tam, guarding the core, refuses him at gunpoint. Emotional beat: the vote repaid; loyalty and truth briefly aligned.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With navies inbound and the array failing, Lena speaks the message herself — the aliens' testimony layered with her own voice, unedited, in every language she knows including the one she dreams. The signal goes out wide and raw. Emotional beat: climax; truth delivered at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Across two fleets, weapons hold as the evidence spreads faster than orders can countermand it. Corvane is arrested by his own security detail; armistice talks reopen under public eye. The Vespera surrenders peacefully, betting on the crowd. Emotional beat: exhausted, trembling victory.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tribunals and pardons interleave; the crew faces charges for the theft of their own ship and receives, mostly, understanding. Tam declines restorative treatment, choosing the years he actually lived. Emotional beat: justice outside the law proving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Noor
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Months later, Lena returns to rebuilt Kestrel-9 — no longer alone, visited by the crew on rotation, the beacon now a monument and a listening post. The signal in her dreams has gone quiet, replaced by ordinary human sleep. Emotional beat: resolution; she was named for light, and finally gets to rest in it.
